sources.entry: JackMate - JackMate is a native macOS app to start, configure and patch the JACK audio server, with a visual patchbay, saved studios and a menu bar mode.

summary.one_liner: JackMate is a native macOS app for starting, configuring, and patching the JACK audio server from the menu bar or a standard window.
summary.what_it_does: JackMate starts and stops the jackd server with a custom configuration covering sample rate, buffer size, I/O device, hog mode, clock drift, and channel selection, and shows the generated command with a copy button. It provides a visual patchbay for connecting JACK clients by dragging between ports, with node grouping, collapse, automatic layout, and multi-selection. Studios save and restore the full session, including JACK parameters, clients, connections, and node positions, and relaunch CLI clients. A JACK transport panel offers play, pause, stop, seek, BBT/HMS/Frames display, and timebase master control. The README also describes JackMoebius integration, which exposes native macOS apps such as Safari or Music as JACK clients with per-app volumes; this requires the separate JackMoebius driver. MIDI via CoreMIDI is marked experimental.
use_cases: start and configure the JACK audio server on a Mac
route audio between applications with a visual patchbay
save and restore audio setups as studios
send native macOS app audio into JACK
manage JACK from the menu bar
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the project's releases
Drag JackMate to the Applications folder and launch it
stack: JACK2 (libjack loaded at runtime via dlopen)
notable: Signed and notarized by Apple with Developer ID, so it opens without Gatekeeper warnings
Visual patchbay with drag-to-connect, automatic Sugiyama/tidy layout, and meta-cables
Studios capture full session state, including JackMoebius exposed apps and per-app volumes
Menu bar mode and standard window mode
Localized in French, English, German, Italian, and Spanish
caveats: Requires macOS 15.0 (Sequoia) or later and a separately installed JACK2
MIDI support via CoreMIDI is experimental; with JACK 1.9.22 stopping takes longer while MIDI is on
JackMoebius is a separate paid driver (free 14-day trial, then one-time purchase), and studios saved with 2.0 need re-saving for the 2.1 format
